 821→    def _attr_lines(n, cap: int) -> list[str]:
 822→        out: list[str] = []
 823→        for k, v in sorted(n.attrs.items(), key=lambda kv: (-_relevance(kv[0], kv[1], asked),
 824→                                                             kv[0])):
 825→            if len(out) >= cap:
 826→                break
 827→            if not _showable(v):
 828→                continue
 829→            atag = _cite(f"{n.id}#{k}", f"{n.label} · {k}", "attribute", [n.source_for(k)],
 830→                         attr=k)
 831→            if atag is None:
 832→                continue
 833→            out.append(f"    {_tags(atag)} {k}: {v}")
 834→        return out
 835→
 836→    def _kind_str(p) -> str:
 837→        return str(getattr(getattr(p, "kind", None), "value", getattr(p, "kind", "")))
 838→
 839→    def _edge_key(e) -> str:
 840→        return f"{e.src_id} --[{e.kind.value}]--> {e.dst_id}"
 841→
 842→    def _field_of(e) -> Optional[str]:
 843→        """``table.column`` the relationship was read from, when its pointer is a table cell."""
 844→        p = next((p for p in e.sources if _kind_str(p) == "table_cell" and p.column), None)
 845→        return f"{p.table}.{p.column}" if p is not None and p.table else (
 846→            p.column if p is not None else None)
 847→
 848→    def _field_edge_lines(n, cap: int) -> list[str]:
 849→        """E2E run 4, Q-03: a field of the matched record's OWN row that ingestion turned into a
 850→        relationship (``customers.account_owner`` -> a ``manages`` edge from the employee) left
 851→        no attribute on the record, so the context said "X --[MANAGES]--> Y" far down the
 852→        RELATIONSHIPS list and nothing under the record called it an account owner — and the
 853→        model answered that the context held none. The field is written under the record, by
 854→        its column name, naming the related record it points at.
 855→
 856→        Which edges qualify is decided by POINTERS, never by kind names: the edge's own pointer
 857→        is a ``table_cell`` on the same ``(source, table, row)`` as one of the record's own
 858→        pointers. A relationship read from ANOTHER row (a contact's ``customer_id``) is not a
 859→        field of this record and stays in RELATIONSHIPS only. The line carries the edge's tag and
 860→        the related record's tag; a related SUBJECT carries its identity caveat — naming who a
 861→        record points at is a citation, never an identification."""
 862→        own = {(p.source_id, p.table, p.row_id)
 863→               for p in [*n.sources, *n.attr_sources.values()]
 864→               if p is not None and _kind_str(p) == "table_cell" and p.row_id is not None}
 865→        if not own:
 866→            return []
 867→        found: dict = {}
 868→        for e in edges_seen:
 869→            if n.id not in (e.src_id, e.dst_id) or e.src_id == e.dst_id:
 870→                continue
 871→            o = by_id.get(e.dst_id if e.src_id == n.id else e.src_id)
 872→            if o is None:
 873→                continue
 874→            p = next((p for p in e.sources if _kind_str(p) == "table_cell" and p.column
 875→                      and (p.source_id, p.table, p.row_id) in own), None)
 876→            if p is None or p.column in n.attrs:
 877→                continue
 878→            found.setdefault((p.column, o.id), (p.column, e, o))
 879→        out: list[str] = []
 880→        for col, e, o in sorted(found.values(),
 881→                                key=lambda t: (-_relevance(t[0], t[2].label, asked), t[0],
 882→                                               t[2].label)):
 883→            if len(out) >= cap:
 884→                break
 885→            etag = _cite(_edge_key(e), f"{by_id[e.src_id].label} → {by_id[e.dst_id].label}",
 886→                         "relationship", e.sources, edge_kind=e.kind.value)
 887→            otag = _cite_node(o)
 888→            if etag is None or otag is None:
 889→                continue
 890→            line = (f"    {_tags(etag, otag)} {col}: {o.label} [{o.kind.value}] (this record's "
 891→                    f"{col} field, held as a {e.kind.value.upper()} relationship from "
 892→                    f"{by_id[e.src_id].label} to {by_id[e.dst_id].label})")
 893→            if is_subject(o.kind):
 894→                line += f"  [{o.label}: IDENTITY — {subject_node_caveat(o.kind)}]"
 895→            out.append(line)
 896→        return out
 897→
 898→    # Relationships the question asks about come first (their kind and the field they were read
 899→    # from, against the asked words), so the 20-line cap below never cuts the one asked for.
 900→    edges_seen.sort(key=lambda e: -_relevance(e.kind.value, _field_of(e) or "", asked))
 901→    lines = [header, "=" * len(header),
 902→             "ENTITIES FOUND (every record the question's words matched, best first; answer from "
 903→             "all of them and say which record each fact comes from):"]
 904→    if records[0] and records[1]:
 905→        lines.append(f"  NOTE: the identifier names {', '.join(repr(n.label) for n in records[0])}"
 906→                     f"; {len(records[1])} other record(s) carry the same identifier and are "
 907→                     f"listed after it as SEPARATE records — answer about the named record.")
 908→    for label, shown, total in neighbourhood_cut:
 909→        lines.append(f"  NOTE: {label!r} has {total} relationships; the {shown} most relevant to "
 910→                     f"the question were read. A relationship not listed below is not shown, "
 911→                     f"not absent.")

1105→def ground_narration(answer: str, context: str) -> dict:
1106→    """Bind every value the narration states to the tagged fact lines that contain it.
1107→
1108→    ``{"bound": [{"token", "tags"}], "unbound": [token, ...]}``. A value is bound only by a line
1109→    ``build_context`` wrote WITH a pointer-backed tag — not by the header, not by the question.
1110→    A value the model took from the question alone is therefore unbound: it is the user's claim,
1111→    and repeating it back is not evidence for it. The model's own ``[C<n>]`` tags are ignored for
1112→    the match; the binding is recomputed, never trusted.

1114→    FIN-08: values are read whole and by kind (``databridge_core.value_forms``). ``33,600,000.00``
1115→    is one number bound by a line holding ``33600000.00``; ``CM-2026-0029`` is one identifier. A
1116→    number of a different value binds to nothing.

1118→    from databridge_core.value_forms import value_spans

1120→    facts = _fact_lines(context)
1121→    bound, unbound, seen = [], [], set()
1122→    for span in value_spans(_FACT_TAG.sub(" ", answer or "")):
1123→        ident = (span.kind, span.key)
1124→        if ident in seen:
1125→            continue
1126→        seen.add(ident)

1128→                      key=lambda t: int(t[1:]))
1129→        if tags:
1130→            bound.append({"token": span.raw, "tags": tags})
1131→        else:
1132→            unbound.append(span.raw)
